title: Adaptive Surge Prober for Mixed-Workload Tokenflow and p95 Regression Detection
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Build a stable, reproducible harness that probes bursty and sustained mixed workloads to quantify how continuous batching and queueing interact with KV prefix cache behavior and produce p95 latency regressions. Unlike prior synthetic-only probes, this harness will emulate short microbursts, long tails of low-rate sessions, and overlapping multi-model mixes while exercising live batching logic and realistic prefix reuse patterns. Outputs will be tokens/sec surfaces, p95 and p99 latency time-series, batch-size distributions, queue-length heatmaps and KV-cache hit/eviction traces for regression detection and root cause correlation.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can replay 3 canonical mixed profiles (microburst-heavy, steady-multi-tenant, cold-start-dominant) and produce reproducible token/sec and p95 surfaces
Automated regression detector flags >95% true positive regressions on injected synthetic slowdowns (kernel slowdown, increased queuing) with <5% false positives over a 24h baseline
Metrics exported to Grafana dashboard and archived to s3://redwood-bench/eng/eng-20684/ with structured CSV + JSON outputs
End-to-end run (30m canonical profile) completes without node OOMs and reports batch-size and KV-cache histograms
Playbook created: steps for reproducing flagged regressions, correlating with kernel scheduling and cache eviction traces
steps: Define three arrival profiles and tenant mixes in arrival-config.yaml (microburst, steady, cold-start-dominant)
Extend tokenflow-synth to emit prefixed session traces that mimic real prefix reuse ratios (70/20/10 hot/warm/cold)
Instrument runtime to emit batch_size, queue_depth, kv_cache_hit, kv_cache_eviction, tokens_emitted, and per-request p95 latency to Prometheus
Add an adaptive concurrency driver that ramps RPS according to observed latency to measure tipping points
Implement regression detection using two-window comparison (baseline 4h, probe 30m) with augmented Bayesian change scoring and z-score alert thresholds
Integrate alerts to #bench-regressions Slack channel and attach run artifacts (logs, traces, CSVs)
Run smoke runs against staging and iterate on thresholds to calibrate false-positive rate
design_notes: Key trade-offs: We prioritize signal-to-noise for p95 detection over raw throughput. To avoid overfitting to a single model size, the harness will run three model configurations: medium (7B), large (30B), and quantized 8-bit variant. To stress KV caching, sessions will include repeated prefixes with controlled inter-arrival gaps to exercise both cache hits and eviction churn. Regression detection uses a hybrid approach: fast z-score for quick alerts and a slower Bayesian method to reduce noise during diurnal traffic changes. We will store runs with deterministic RNG seeds so identical mixes can be re-run for RCA.
risks: False positives from diurnal variability if baseline window overlaps production-like load shifts
Large storage cost if we retain full trace dumps for every run; we will sample traces instead
Instrumentation might add 2-5% CPU/GPU overhead, biasing some microbenchmarks
Edge cases where eviction traces are incomplete due to in-memory compaction in runtime
blockers: Need runtime metric endpoint for kv_cache_eviction (ENG-20910) - dependency
Access to a staging fleet with mixed-model images and quantized runtime (ops approval required)
